newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain govt mulls 3 pct electricity price cut.
newsitem.headline: Spain govt mulls 3 pct electricity price cut.

text.p: Spain's Industry and Energy Ministry is considering an average three percent reduction in electricity charges in 1997, a spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.

"The Ministry is studying a possible real reduction of three percent in the electricity tariff, which would above all affect small and medium-sized firms, while the cut for household users will be less," the spokesman said.
"The Ministry is studying this new scheme but we also have to think about compensatory measures so the (electricity) utilities (affected) are not punished on the stock market," he said.
A meeting is due to take place mid-September between the Ministry and representatives of the electricity firms to discuss possible changes to the sector.

The new price scheme might mean a cut of around one percent in domestic electricity charges, up to five percent for small- and medium-sized businesses and a tariff freeze for industrial users, he said.
No decision has been made as yet but the new charges will be agreed before year end, the spokesman said.
